title: Should You Establish a Limited Liability Company or a Joint Stock Company?
description: A practical comparison of ownership, capital raising and governance before choosing a company structure in Vietnam.
intro: The right structure should reflect how the founders intend to own, finance and manage the business—not simply which registration file looks shorter.

sections.heading: When an LLC is a practical choice
paragraphs: A limited liability company is often suitable for a closely held business with a defined group of owners. Transfers can be more controlled, and the governance structure is generally easier to operate.
bullets: One owner or a limited group of members

sections.heading: When a joint stock company fits better
paragraphs: A joint stock company is designed for a business that expects a broader shareholder base or future capital raising. That flexibility comes with more formal governance and record-keeping.
bullets: More suitable for multiple investment rounds

sections.heading: Decide before filing
paragraphs: Confirm the intended owners, transfer restrictions, fundraising plan and decision-making model. Changing structure later is possible, but it can affect contracts, tax records and internal approvals.

takeaway: Choose the structure around the next stage of the business, not only the day of incorporation.

title: What Documents Are Needed to Establish a Company in Vietnam?
description: The information and documents founders should align before preparing an enterprise registration application.
intro: A complete application starts with consistent information. Names, addresses, business lines, capital and ownership details should match across every document.

sections.heading: Company information
paragraphs: Prepare the proposed Vietnamese name, head-office address, business lines, charter capital and details of the legal representative. The address and regulated activities should be checked before filing.

sections.heading: Owner and shareholder documents
paragraphs: Identity or legal-status documents are required for individual and organizational owners. Foreign-issued documents may require consular legalization and Vietnamese translation, depending on the case.

sections.heading: Registration documents and final review
paragraphs: The application normally includes the registration form, charter and lists or authorization documents relevant to the selected structure.
bullets: Use the same spelling and identification details throughout
Check document validity and required attachments
Retain a complete signed filing set

takeaway: Build one verified information sheet first, then generate every application document from that source.

title: Charter Capital: How Much Should a New Company Register?
description: How to set charter capital based on operating needs, funding commitments and sector-specific requirements.
intro: Charter capital is a legal and commercial commitment. A figure that is unrealistically high or too low can both create avoidable problems.

sections.heading: Minimum capital is not universal
paragraphs: Many ordinary business lines do not prescribe a fixed minimum. Certain regulated sectors, however, may require legal capital, deposits or proof of financial capacity.

sections.heading: Use operational assumptions
paragraphs: Estimate initial expenses, working capital, contractual commitments and the owners’ actual ability to contribute. Consider how the declared amount will appear to banks, partners and licensing authorities.

sections.heading: Track contribution and later changes
paragraphs: Owners should contribute capital within the applicable statutory period and keep evidence of payment. If plans materially change, review whether a capital adjustment and related corporate actions are needed.

takeaway: Register an amount that is supportable, traceable and appropriate for the planned activity.

title: Registered Office Address: What to Check Before Filing
description: Key legal and operational checks for a company’s registered office in Vietnam.
intro: An address is more than a line on the enterprise certificate. It affects registration, tax administration, licensing and official correspondence.

sections.heading: The address must be identifiable
paragraphs: Use a complete address that can be located within the administrative system. Confirm current ward and city information and avoid ambiguous floor or unit details.

sections.heading: Document the right to use the premises
paragraphs: Keep the lease, ownership evidence or other lawful-use documents. Regulated activities may require additional conditions relating to area, safety or facilities.

sections.heading: Check residential and future-change issues
paragraphs: Apartments designated solely for residential use are generally not appropriate as company offices. A later relocation may require updates with registration, tax, banking, licensing and counterparties.

takeaway: Verify both the legal status and practical suitability of the premises before using the address in an application.

title: What a Company Should Do After Incorporation
description: A structured post-incorporation checklist covering capital, tax, accounting, invoices, employment and operating licences.
intro: Receiving an enterprise registration certificate is the start of the operating phase. The next tasks should be assigned and tracked from day one.

sections.heading: Complete corporate and capital records
paragraphs: Issue internal appointment and governance documents, establish statutory records and monitor capital contributions with suitable payment evidence.

sections.heading: Set up tax, accounting and transactions
paragraphs: Confirm the accounting framework, electronic tax access, digital signature, invoice process and bank account workflow before routine transactions begin.

sections.heading: Review people, data and sector licences
paragraphs: Employment, social insurance, personal-data processing and sector-specific conditions may create separate obligations. These should be mapped to the actual operating model.

takeaway: Use a dated compliance checklist with a named owner for each post-incorporation task.

title: Conditional Business Lines: What Must a Company Verify?
description: How to distinguish enterprise registration from the licences and operating conditions required for regulated activities.
intro: Having a business line recorded does not automatically authorize a company to conduct every regulated activity within it.

sections.heading: Check three layers
paragraphs: Review market-access rules, sector licences and ongoing operating conditions. Requirements may relate to capital, personnel, premises, equipment or professional certificates.

sections.heading: Registration is not a substitute for a licence
paragraphs: Enterprise registration records the intended activity. Where specialist law requires approval, the company should obtain it and satisfy the conditions before commencing that activity.

sections.heading: Prepare evidence and maintain compliance
paragraphs: Create a document list for each condition and identify who maintains it after licensing. Some conditions must remain satisfied throughout operation, not only on the filing date.

takeaway: Map every intended revenue-generating activity to its licence and compliance requirements before launch.

title: Foreign Investors Establishing a Company in Vietnam: A Practical Roadmap
description: The main review and registration stages from market access to investment and enterprise registration.
intro: A foreign-invested project should be structured around the investor, activity, location, capital and implementation schedule before documents are drafted.

sections.heading: Review market access and project conditions
paragraphs: Confirm whether the proposed activity is open, conditional or restricted for foreign investors. Ownership limits, partner requirements and sector approvals may affect the structure.

sections.heading: Prepare investment registration
paragraphs: Depending on the project, an investment policy approval may be required before or alongside investment registration. Financial capacity, premises and implementation assumptions should be supported by documents.

sections.heading: Register the enterprise and activate operations
paragraphs: After the relevant investment step, complete enterprise registration and post-licensing tasks such as capital accounts, capital contribution, tax, accounting and specialist licences.
bullets: Align investor names across foreign and Vietnamese documents
Allow time for legalization and translation

takeaway: Resolve market access and project structure first; document preparation should follow those decisions.

title: When Must an Investment Registration Certificate Be Amended?
description: Changes that should trigger a review of the Investment Registration Certificate and related enterprise records.
intro: A project evolves over time. Material changes should be reviewed before implementation so that approvals and actual operations remain aligned.

sections.heading: Changes that commonly require review
paragraphs: Investor, project name, location, objectives, scale, capital, duration and implementation schedule are typical areas that may affect the investment registration record.

sections.heading: Coordinate investment and enterprise information
paragraphs: A single transaction can affect both the Investment Registration Certificate and enterprise registration. The order of filings should be planned to avoid inconsistent records.

sections.heading: Explain feasibility and prepare evidence
paragraphs: The amendment file should clearly state the reason, approval basis and ability to implement the revised project. Financial, premises and progress documents may be relevant.

takeaway: Review the complete transaction—not one certificate in isolation—before deciding the filing sequence.

title: Changing Enterprise Registration Details: What Should a Company Do?
description: A practical workflow for changes to company name, address, capital, business lines, representatives and ownership records.
intro: A registered change affects more than the enterprise database. Contracts, licences, invoices, banking and public information may need coordinated updates.

sections.heading: Identify the change and approval authority
paragraphs: Common changes include company name, head office, business lines, charter capital, legal representative, members or shareholders. Internal approval must follow the charter and applicable law.

sections.heading: Determine the filing route
paragraphs: Some matters require registration of a change; others are handled by notification or by updating internal records. Filing deadlines and supporting resolutions should be checked for the specific event.

sections.heading: Update connected systems
paragraphs: After the registration step, review tax, invoices, bank accounts, digital signatures, licences, contracts, websites and personal-data notices.

takeaway: Use one change-control checklist covering corporate approval, filing and every connected operational record.

title: Transferring Capital Contributions or Shares: Key Issues to Review
description: Corporate, investment, contractual and tax checks for a transfer of company ownership interests.
intro: A transfer is not complete merely because the parties sign a contract. Restrictions, payment, tax and registration consequences must work together.

sections.heading: Confirm the right to transfer
paragraphs: Review the charter, shareholder or member agreements, statutory priority rights and any approval requirements. Existing pledges or disputes should also be checked.

sections.heading: Review the incoming investor and transaction terms
paragraphs: Foreign ownership or conditional sectors may trigger investment procedures. The agreement should clearly state the interest transferred, price, payment method, completion conditions and allocation of risk.

sections.heading: Handle tax and post-closing updates
paragraphs: Assess declaration and payment obligations for the relevant transferor. After completion, update member or shareholder records, beneficial information, enterprise or investment registrations where required, and related internal documents.

takeaway: Plan signing, payment, tax and registration as one closing process with defined conditions and evidence.

title: Establishing an FDI Company in Vietnam in 2026: Process and Documents
description: A guide to market-access conditions, investment registration, enterprise registration and post-licensing work for a foreign-invested company in Vietnam.
intro: Establishing a foreign-invested company involves more than registering a legal entity. Market access, project structure, ownership, location, capital, foreign exchange and sector licences must work together.

sections.heading: Two routes into the market
paragraphs: An investor may establish a new economic organization linked to an investment project or acquire capital in an existing Vietnamese enterprise. A new entity offers structural control; an acquisition requires careful legal, tax and operational due diligence.

sections.heading: Checks before documents are drafted
paragraphs: Review ownership limits, investment form, permitted scope and specialist conditions for the proposed activities. Investor structure, capital, contribution schedule and project location should be supported by realistic evidence.

sections.heading: Registration process
paragraphs: First define the entity type, ownership, representative, activities, location, capital and schedule. Determine whether investment policy approval is required, then complete investment registration where applicable and enterprise registration with consistent information.

sections.heading: Investor documents
paragraphs: Individual investors commonly prepare passports and evidence of financial capacity. Corporate investors generally need incorporation records, constitutional documents, financial statements, investment approvals and representative documents. Foreign-issued documents may require legalization and Vietnamese translation.

sections.heading: Post-licensing work
paragraphs: Set up the appropriate capital account, contribute capital correctly and establish tax, accounting, invoicing, employment and investment-reporting processes. Regulated activities should begin only after the necessary licences or operating conditions are in place.

takeaway: Resolve the investment structure, activities, capital and location before drafting; preparation quality largely determines the practical timeline.

title: Foreign-Invested Enterprises in Vietnam: Structure, Formation and Compliance
description: An overview of how foreign-invested enterprises are formed and how market access, capital, accounts and ongoing obligations are managed.
intro: A foreign-invested enterprise is not a separate company type. It is organized under Vietnamese enterprise law, while the foreign element arises from the status and ownership of its investors.

sections.heading: What is a foreign-invested enterprise?
paragraphs: It is an economic organization with a foreign investor as a member or shareholder. Obligations should not be assessed only by reference to a 50% ownership threshold; any foreign participation can create investment, market-access and foreign-exchange issues.

sections.heading: How it can be formed
paragraphs: The enterprise may be newly established for an investment project, created through a capital or share acquisition, or converted from a domestic enterprise after a foreign investment transaction. Acquiring an operating company also means taking on its historical risks.

sections.heading: Company type and market access
paragraphs: LLCs offer more concentrated ownership control, while a joint stock company suits broader fundraising. Before registration or acquisition, check ownership limits, permitted activities, investment form, partner requirements and sector conditions.

sections.heading: Capital and cross-border payments
paragraphs: Charter capital and total project investment are related but distinct. Contributions, transfers, foreign loans and profit remittances must use the correct account, party, currency and timing under foreign-exchange rules.

sections.heading: Ongoing obligations
paragraphs: In addition to tax, accounting, employment and corporate governance, the enterprise may need to manage investment reports, project milestones, specialist licences and foreign employees. Material changes should be reviewed across both investment and enterprise records.

takeaway: Foreign ownership affects the business from market entry through capital transactions and operations; investment and corporate records should be managed as one system.

title: Establishing a Representative Office of a Foreign Company in Vietnam in 2026
description: Conditions, documents, permitted activities and post-licensing obligations for a foreign company’s representative office in Vietnam.
intro: A representative office suits a foreign trader that wants to research the market, build partnerships and support its head office without directly generating revenue in Vietnam.

sections.heading: What is a representative office?
paragraphs: It is a dependent unit of a foreign trader licensed in Vietnam for liaison, market research and promotion. It is not an independent enterprise and may not directly sell goods, supply services or generate revenue in Vietnam.

sections.heading: Licensing conditions
paragraphs: The foreign trader must be lawfully established and generally have operated for at least one year. Its remaining registration term and the proposed office activities must meet the applicable requirements and Vietnam’s international commitments.

sections.heading: Permitted scope
paragraphs: The office may act as a contact point, research the market, identify partners, promote the head office and monitor contracts signed by the foreign trader. A revenue-generating model should be structured as a company or, where appropriate, a branch.

sections.heading: Application documents
paragraphs: The file generally includes the application, the head office’s registration document, appointment of the chief representative, evidence of continuing operation, identity documents and premises records. Foreign documents may require legalization, translation and certification.

sections.heading: After licensing
paragraphs: Complete tax-code, bank-account, staffing, employment, signage and record-keeping steps, and maintain the required activity reports. Work-permit and residence procedures for a foreign chief representative are separate from the office licence.

takeaway: A representative office is designed for liaison, research and promotion; the structure must match the actual activity rather than simply the easiest initial filing.
